The amount of snow that falls in a year

questions.q: The chapter ends: 'The diverse ways in which humans have made all landforms their home is a testimony to our adaptability and resilience.' Justify this with one example each from mountains, plateaus, plains and deserts, and explain what resilience means.
questions.a: Resilience is the capacity to meet challenges and difficulties, adapt to them or overcome them. Mountains: on rugged, steep slopes people cut terraces, herd animals and run tourism despite avalanches, landslides and cloudbursts. Plateaus: where rocky soil makes farming less favourable, people mine the rich mineral deposits, as in Chhota Nagpur. Plains: people farm the fertile soil and, in recent decades, irrigated it, while facing groundwater depletion. Deserts: despite harsh conditions and little precipitation, humans have adapted to most deserts, and Thar communities keep rich traditions of folk songs and legends.
s: Meaning of resilience
Mountain example of adapting to the land and its hazards
Plateau example: mining where farming is hard
Plains example: farming and irrigation with its challenge
Desert example: adapting to the Thar and its traditions

questions.q:
A museum gallery on 'Land and life in Tamil Sangam poetry' has notes on five imaginary settlements.
S1: a hill village whose people gather honey and forest fruit and hunt.
S2: a camp of cattle herders at the edge of a forest and grassland.
S3: a village of rice fields on rich, flat river land.
S4: a harbour town with fishing boats and ships.
S5: a halt for travellers crossing dry, sandy country.
(a) Which tinai fits S2, and which fits S5?
(b) The chapter's own landform sections (mountains, plateaus, plains, deserts) mention hills and mountains, forests and grasslands, fertile river plains, and dry deserts. Which ONE settlement's landscape is not named anywhere in those sections?
(c) Judge whether the settlement in (b) shows that the three-landform scheme is wrong, or that the two schemes have different purposes. Use what each scheme is based on.
questions.a: (a) S2 is Mullai (grassland and forests, cattle rearing); S5 is Palai (arid, desert-like land, journeying). (b) S4, the harbour town: coastal land is not named in any landform section, while S1 fits mountains, S2's forests and grasslands are named in the mountain environment, S3 fits plains and S5 fits deserts. (c) Different purposes, not wrong. The three main landforms are told apart by height and shape, and the chapter itself says the surface is complex and experts define a few more landforms; the tinais group land by landscape and the main occupation, so a coast with fishing and seafaring is a natural group there.
s: (a) S2 Mullai, S5 Palai
(b) S4, the coastal harbour town
(c) Judges the schemes have different bases (height and shape versus landscape and occupation)

questions.q: Town A gets heavy snow every winter and showers in summer. Town B gets rain on only a few days a year and no snow. Which town fits the chapter's description of a desert better, and why?
questions.a: Town B, since deserts get very little precipitation of any kind
o: Town B, since deserts get very little precipitation of any kind
Town A, since deserts are cold and snow falls only in deserts
Town A, since snow is not precipitation and does not count
Town B, since every desert is hot, just as the Sahara and the Thar are

questions.q:
Each person in Column A lives in one tinai landscape of ancient Tamil Sangam poetry. Match each person with the tinai in Column B, using the landscape and the work described.
Column A: 1. a family that collects wild honey and hunts on high, rugged slopes  2. herders whose cows graze between woods and open meadows  3. boat-builders whose catch comes from the sea  4. a caravan crossing sun-baked, dry country
Column B: a. Mullai  b. Neydal  c. Kurinji  d. Palai

Write two short descriptions of imaginary villages, one for Mullai and one for Palai, so that a reader could name the tinai from the landscape and the work alone (do not use the tinai names). Then state the one clue that most clearly separates the two.
questions.a: Sample. Mullai: 'Families live at the edge of a forest beside open grassland and keep herds of cattle.' Palai: 'In this dry, sandy land, men set out on long journeys and the village keeps fighters to guard its routes.' Clue: grassland and forest with cattle rearing versus arid, desert-like land with journeying and fighting.
s: A Mullai village with grassland or forest and cattle rearing
A Palai village with arid land and journeying or fighting
States the separating clue of landscape and occupation

questions.q: The chapter says you need not remember the details of the tinais, 'but the concepts they reflect need to be understood'. (a) State one concept the tinais reflect. (b) Show that concept with one tinai from the table.
questions.a: (a) The deep connection between humanity and the natural environment: the kind of land shapes how people live (a keen awareness of diverse regions). (b) Example: Neydal, the coastal region, goes with fishing and seafaring (or Mullai, grassland and forests, with cattle rearing).
s: (a) Landscape and human life are deeply connected
(b) One tinai whose occupation follows from its landscape

questions.q: (a) The chapter calls the flora and fauna of deserts 'unique'. A student says this means deserts have almost no plants or animals. Correct her. (b) Give two features from the chapter that together set deserts apart as a landform of their own.
questions.a: (a) 'Unique' means special to deserts, unlike those of other landforms; it does not mean that deserts have none. (b) Deserts are large, dry expanses with very little precipitation, and their flora and fauna are unique.
s: (a) Unique means special to deserts, not absent
(b) Large dry expanse with very little precipitation, and unique flora and fauna

questions.q: A student must place the Thar Desert, a large, dry expanse with very little precipitation, in the chapter's scheme of landforms. Which placement fits the chapter?
questions.a: As a desert, one of a few more landforms experts define
o: As a desert, one of a few more landforms experts define
As a plain, since much of its land is flat and lies quite low
As a plateau, since deserts rise above the land nearby
Nowhere, since humans have not adapted to any desert

questions.q: In the tinai table, the number of landscape descriptions that contain the name of one of the chapter's three main landforms (mountain, plateau, plain) is ___.
True or False? 'All deserts are hot.' Give the verdict and the correction.
questions.a: False. Deserts are large, dry expanses with very little precipitation; some are hot, like the Sahara and the Thar, but others are cold, like the Gobi Desert in Asia.
s: Verdict: False
Correction: dryness defines deserts; the Gobi is a cold desert

questions.q:
A desert village in northwest India has families who farm a little near a well and others who move with their camels and sheep across the dry land for months each year. Rain falls on only a few days a year. At a district fair, their folk troupe sings songs about wells, sand and journeys. A visitor remarks: 'Most people of this desert are just passing through it; it has no settled life of its own.'
(a) Which desert of the chapter is this village most likely in, and is it a hot or a cold desert?
(b) Which feature of deserts in the chapter makes living conditions here harsh?
(c) Which tinai's landscape and occupation are closest to the life of the families who move across the dry land?
(d) Which part of the visitor's remark does the chapter support, and which part does it not? Judge, using (c) and the troupe.
questions.a: (a) The Thar Desert, a hot desert in the northwest of the Indian Subcontinent. (b) Deserts are large, dry expanses with very little precipitation. (c) Palai: arid, desert-like regions with journeying (and fighting). (d) Partly right. The chapter does speak of communities migrating through the Thar, as the moving families show. But it also speaks of communities living in the Thar, and says humans have adapted to most deserts; the village's farming families and their folk songs and legends are a settled culture tied to the desert. So 'no settled life of its own' is wrong.
s: (a) The Thar, a hot desert
(b) Very little precipitation in a large, dry expanse
(c) Palai, with journeying
(d) Partly right: migration through the Thar is real, but communities also live there with their own traditions

questions.q:
Assertion (A): In the tinai table, Neydal is linked with fishing and seafaring.
Reason (R): Each tinai pairs a landscape with the work its people mainly do, and Neydal's landscape is the coast.
questions.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

questions.q: A poster sorts the deserts named in the chapter into 'Hot' and 'Cold' columns. If Antarctica, which is very cold and gets little snowfall, is also added as some experts suggest, the 'Cold' column will have ___ entries.

The chapter's summary says each landform offers different challenges as well as opportunities. (a) For plains, show that one change in farming brought both an opportunity and a challenge. (b) For plateaus, show that the same rocky land is a challenge for one activity but an opportunity for another.
questions.a: (a) The turn from rainfed farming to irrigation increased agricultural production (opportunity) but has also contributed to the depletion of groundwater (challenge). (b) Rocky plateau soil is less fertile than plains, so it is less favourable to farming (challenge), but plateaus are rich in mineral deposits, so mining is a major activity on them (opportunity).
s: (a) Irrigation raised production but depleted groundwater
(b) Rocky soil hampers farming, but minerals make mining a major activity

questions.q: (a) Which tinai links fertile agricultural plains with farming, and which part of the chapter agrees with it? (b) The chapter's plains section names two major occupations of the Ganga plain. Name the one that this tinai's entry leaves out.
questions.a: (a) Marudam; the plains section also says fertile floodplains are ideal for crops, and agriculture is a major occupation. (b) River fishing.
s: (a) Marudam, matching the plains section on farming
(b) River fishing
